PullRequest.Title: agentHost: run known regressions as strict expected failures
PullRequest.Body:

Adds `assertExpectedFailure(issue, expectedError, run)`: a matching failure passes; a different error or unexpected success fails.

This makes it easier to confirm an issue exists with a test, keep running it while broken, and know when to enforce the fix. Applied to the existing managed-telemetry regression for [github/copilot-agent-runtime#24069](https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/pull/24069).

Example when an SDK roll fixes the issue:

```text
Unexpected pass for github/copilot-agent-runtime#24069. Remove the expected-failure marker and keep the desired-behavior assertions.
```

<details>
<summary>Validation: 14 unit tests and 5 integration tests passing locally</summary>

macOS arm64, bundled SDK; cross-platform CI pending.

- `npm run gulp compile-client` and `npm run precommit` — passed.
- `VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH=1 ./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2eExpectedFailure.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/capiReplayProxy.test.ts` — 14 passing.
- `VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH=1 ./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/copilotOtelAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts` — 5 passing.

</details>

Scenarios.Scenario: Normal replay run of the managed-telemetry integration suite now executes the known-failure no-restart case by default.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Per-test setup must create isolated directories, bind the loopback OTLP receiver, launch the agent-host/replay stack, complete one recorded model turn and telemetry assertion, observe the second session's expected configuration failure, dispose both sessions, and stop local resources before the test completes. Recording mode still skips this case.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launches one in-tree agent-host child for this test lease; first provider use can initialize the cached bundled Copilot runtime used by both sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One agent-host launch for the newly enabled test, with one provider runtime reused across its two serial session attempts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The entire scenario, including its process startup, was skipped unless AGENT_HOST_RUN_KNOWN_ISSUES=1.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Startup and shutdown are on the integration test's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Uses loopback AHP, replay/model, managed-settings, and OTLP HTTP endpoints; one model response is consumed and the second fixture response remains intentionally unused after the expected session-creation failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Fixed per execution: two serial session attempts, one completed model turn, two policy refreshes, and bounded local telemetry traffic. No external network is reached in replay mode.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These loopback requests did not occur in default runs because the test was opt-in.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The first turn and its OTLP export must finish; the second attempt must reach the expected local failure.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Creates a temporary workspace/cache, removes the managed-settings cache for each policy change, reads the two-exchange fixture, and removes temporary state in teardown.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A fixed number of operations for one added test execution; two policy-cache removals and one isolated directory lifecycle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Absent from default runs while the case was gated behind AGENT_HOST_RUN_KNOWN_ISSUES.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Setup, policy invalidation, fixture loading, and teardown are awaited on the test path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One additional test per invocation/platform shard of this integration file; the fixture has exactly two exchanges and the scenario does not scale with repositories, files, users, or history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two session attempts are serial. The agent-host child, replay HTTP server, mock model server, and OTLP receiver run concurrently as services, but requests are awaited and there is no per-item concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The test uses a fresh cache home and explicitly evicts managed settings before each policy. The replay fixture is loaded locally; within the test the provider runtime is warm for the second session, but the test lease is disposed afterward. There is no cross-run cache or miss retry fan-out.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that default CI now pays one extra child-process-backed replay scenario; high confidence that it remains bounded to one successful turn and one expected failing session.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact process startup and telemetry export time varies by CI platform, but cardinality is fixed and local. The maximum test timeout is not evidence of normal duration.
Scenarios.Verdict: This intentionally adds bounded integration-test latency to detect when the upstream regression is fixed. It does not create an input-scaled or product-runtime performance regression, so no finding is warranted.

Scenarios.Scenario: CapiReplayProxy expected-failure verification unit cases exercise record/replay behavior for three failure states.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each case creates a temporary fixture, records two local responses, starts a replay proxy, sends one replay request, verifies strict and relaxed mismatch behavior, closes servers, and removes the directory.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Starts loopback record and replay HTTP servers and performs local fetches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three cases; each records two requests and performs one replay request, for nine bounded loopback fetches total.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These three cases and their local HTTP operations did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All local fetches and server closes are awaited by their unit test.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Creates, writes/reads, and removes one small two-exchange fixture per case.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three temporary directory/fixture lifecycles with constant-size payloads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fixture persistence and cleanup are on each unit test's path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly three enumerated failure modes with two recorded exchanges each; no unbounded input controls multiplicity.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The loop-generated Mocha tests execute as separate serial cases; requests within each case are serial.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each test uses an isolated cold fixture and proxy; no shared cache, retry loop, or negative-cache behavior is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the added I/O counts from the loop and explicit fetches.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Local filesystem and loopback timings vary, but the tiny fixed cardinality makes material suite degradation unlikely.
Scenarios.Verdict: The added test work is small and strictly bounded; it does not meet the threshold for an actionable performance regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Expected-failure helper and replay release verification run across unit tests and existing E2E teardown paths.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The helper awaits one supplied operation, checks one Error message, and writes a short line only for the expected failure. Lease release still performs session cleanup and one replay-bucket verification before resource shutdown.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Helper cost is constant per invocation. Replay verification remains linear in the current fixture's bucket count, exactly as before; the new option only suppresses reporting of unused responses for the one recognized failure.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single awaited operation per helper call; teardown remains serial per created session as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is added. Replay buckets retain their existing per-fixture reset and disposal lifecycle; misses and mismatches are still checked.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete helper and teardown call path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; only constant-sized Error/RegExp work and existing teardown scanning are involved.
Scenarios.Verdict: No repeated expensive work, retention, or cleanup regression is introduced.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 8 changed files and every diff page. Traced the newly default integration case through filesystem setup, child-process launch, local replay/model/OTLP traffic, cache behavior, serial session attempts, and cleanup; also reviewed the new proxy/helper unit tests and verification-option paths. The PR adds bounded test-suite work but no actionable product or scaling performance regression.
